Hey [~accountid:5ecceffac761b10c33d5ba08] !

BB team is working on an integration with [Pleo|https://www.pleo.io/en/lp/all], whereby a company's employees can use Pleo cards to pay for their rides. They then assign the ride and cost to the correct cost centre etc in the company's Pleo integration. It's very much us indicating that this person took this ride for them to be able to manage their costs internally. 

User has a specific payment card which they used for their rides. If the ride meets certain criteria (they use Pleo card and if it was taken with a work profile) we have to send certain data to Pleo so they can know if it's one of their cards. We would send:

* First six digits of the credit card number
* Last four digits of the credit card number
* user email address
_(We would only send this if the first six digits belong to a Pleo card. The email address is needed as the last four digits can belong to multiple accounts)_

This is not a typical Bolt Business integration set-up and I haven’t had previous experience to rely on here. 

Pleo foresees a controller-processor set up here. Deeming Bolt as processors for the “Data Services” provided (the term Data Services is described in the Main Agreement, which we do not have at the moment). However the “Data Services” should be limited only to providing (transferring) details of user’s using Pleo card for the payment of their rides. It should be clear that if Bolt processes personal data for its own purposes, then we are an independent controller. 

It does make sense that Bolt is deemed as a processor (we only provide this data under controller’s instructions and on their behalf for them to assign costs). Also, it is the controller’s (Pleo) obligation to ensure that data subjects are informed that when using such cards on Bolt platform then Bolt provides details etc. The DPA needs a check whether we can comply with such processor requirements stipulated or would a controller-controller set up make more sense with the envisaged setup. 

Also we would need to review this together with the Main Agreement (once we receive this).

[AWS docs for MM|https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/multi-model-endpoints.html]

* If the model is already loaded in the container's memory, invocation is faster because SageMaker doesn't need to download and load it.
* SageMaker continues to route requests for a model to the instance where the model is already loaded. However, if the model receives many invocation requests, and there are additional instances for the multi-model endpoint, SageMaker routes some requests to another instance to accommodate the traffic. If the model isn't already loaded on the second instance, the model is downloaded to that instance's storage volume and loaded into the container's memory.
* When an instance's memory utilization is high and SageMaker needs to load another model into memory, it unloads unused models from that instance's container to ensure that there is enough memory to load the model.
* By default, multi-model endpoints cache frequently used models in memory and on disk to provide low latency inference.
* For both CPU and GPU backed instances, have some "slack" memory available so that unused models can be unloaded, and especially for multi-model endpoints with multiple instances. If an instance or an Availability Zone fails, the models on those instances will be rerouted to other instances behind the endpoint.
* In some cases, you might opt to reduce costs by choosing an instance type that can't hold all of the targeted models in memory at once. SageMaker dynamically unloads models when it runs out of memory to make room for a newly targeted model.

*New project - Knowledge Base improvements* 

Hi! 👋  The CS Content team has started work on our project Knowledge Base improvements.

*Current state of the KB*
While our KB is rich with information useful for CS on their daily activities, we understand that there are various difficulties one may encounter:
Sometimes it’s difficult or time-consuming to find relevant information in Beehive
There are different kinds of articles in the KB (e.g. processes, product or tool feature guides, general guidelines, market info) but we don’t have an aligned approach for presenting each type of content
Not all processes are short and sweet - some of them contain lots of additional information and guidelines, presenting them differently may make it easier to follow the processes.

*What we want to achieve*
Design the KB in a way that’s easier for agents and other users to navigate and find relevant information
Create processes that are easy to follow

*What we’ll do*
By end of March, we aim to complete the evaluation of the current KB, figure out how we’d want to redesign it, and collect feedback on the KB usability from the main KB users: CS agents.
By mid-Summer, we plan to go through our initial redesign plan with the user feedback insights in mind, adjust the plans as needed, and start updating the KB.
During this project, our team will focus on the KB changes we can fully control, and any feedback about functionality that we might consider for the future will be provided to the relevant teams. 

*What’s :next: ?* For now, we simply wanted to raise awareness about this project. This is quite a large project and we can’t share a very specific timeline yet - but we’ll share more details when we have further updates and when your input will be needed! :slightly_smiling_face:

Hi, sorry for the delay.

So the reason why the report took so long to load was because we scan the whole data (all historical orders from all market) for a single run, which takes a lot of resource. There is no simple solution with good user experience to resolve this issue, so I prioritize *performance* & *accuracy* at the expense of user experience.

The solution is by adding a new filter, called *Date Partition Range Filter*

This date partition range is a filter used to limit the amount of data to scan. The difference between *Date Partition Range Filter* to *Period Filter* is the purpose: period filter is a business-logic filter i.e. the transaction period you wish to see. On the other hand, date partition range filter is technical filter, a field used to limit the data to be read. In general, if you want to use period filter from *DATE A* to *DATE B*, set the date partition range filter to *DATE A - 60 DAYS* to *DATE B + 20 DAYS*. 

Period filter refers to the timestamp when the order price review is finished (the actual timestamp in the balance entry), while date partition range filter refers to the timestamp of the order creation. If driver disputes the final price, they could file a complaint and Bolt will reassess the price. This could take a while, but most of them don't take more than 2 months (hence, 60 days).

Hope that helps!

Regards,
Ammar

_Bolt takes its law enforcement cooperation responsibilities seriously and rest assured it is always the intention of Bolt to disclose personal data to the police wherever it is permitted and it is appropriate to do so._ 

_We trust you understand that any disclosure of personal data from Bolt for law enforcement purposes must still comply with the GDPR, and in particular, a lawful basis is required under Art.6. The disclosure must be necessary and proportionate to the stated purpose and the disclosure needs to be connected to the investigated issue._

_The nature of the request is exploratory, the threshold of criminality is unknown, and the link mentioned between requested data points with criminal activity to Bolt operations is not specified. The potential, even inadvertent, loss of those third party's right to privacy must be warranted in these circumstances, and the use or intention of that data upon disclosure must be explained (at least at a high level)._

_Bolt, therefore cannot test for necessity and proportionality nor undertake and document an assessment for lawful disclosure - as required by law. In short, compliance with the current disclosure request conflicts with other legal obligations with which Bolt is required to comply i.e. data protection._

_We kindly ask you to provide further information on the reasoning why information is requested, how it pertains to the investigation of the alleged crime (on a high level), nature of the crime (on a high level). Let’s try this query, which should find bookings with initially failed payment:

{code:sql}select
b.id booking_id,
b.created,
bi.payment_method_type,
b.capture_amount_total,
b.payment_collection_status,
b.uncovered_amount,
bi.captured_amount,
p.state,
p.unallocated_amount,
case
    when failed_payment_task.id is not null then failed_payment_task.ignore_until
    when payment_task.ignore_until > fuse_task.ignore_until then fuse_task.ignore_until
    when payment_transfer.amount < least(b.capture_amount_total, bi.captured_amount) then payment_task.ignore_until
    when payment_task.id is null AND fuse_task.ignore_until < now() then fuse_task.ignore_until
end as payment_failed_ts
from glue.ng_balance_user.balance_user_billing_transaction bt
join glue.ng_balance_user.balance_user_booking b on b.transaction_id=bt.id
join glue.ng_balance_user.balance_user_task fuse_task on fuse_task.data_id=b.id
  and fuse_task.data_type='booking'
  and fuse_task.type='capture_booking_fuse'
join glue.ng_balance_user.balance_user_booking_item bi on bi.booking_id=b.id
  and bi.payment_method_type<>'bolt_credit'
join glue.ng_balance_user.balance_user_payment p on p.relation_id=bi.id
  and p.relation_type='booking_item'
  and p.reason='booking_item_payment'
left join glue.ng_balance_user.balance_user_transfer payment_transfer on payment_transfer.related_transaction_id=bt.id
  and payment_transfer.transfer_reason='payment_captured'
  and payment_transfer.created > date '2023-01-01'
left join glue.ng_balance_user.balance_user_task payment_task on payment_task.data_id=payment_transfer.id
  and payment_task.data_type='transfer'
  and payment_task.type in ('payment_finished_api', 'payment_finished_event')
  and payment_task.created > date '2023-01-01'
left join glue.ng_balance_user.balance_user_task failed_payment_task on failed_payment_task.data_id=b.id
  and failed_payment_task.data_type='booking'
  and failed_payment_task.type='payment_finished_event'
  and failed_payment_task.created > date '2023-01-01'
where bt.is_active
and bt.country_code='ee'
and b.state='captured'

and bt.created > date '2023-01-01'
and b.created > date '2023-01-01'
and fuse_task.created > date '2023-01-01'

and (
  failed_payment_task.id is not null
  OR
  (payment_task.ignore_until > fuse_task.ignore_until)
  OR
  (payment_transfer.amount < least(b.capture_amount_total, bi.captured_amount))
  OR
  (payment_task.id is null AND fuse_task.ignore_until < now())
  );{code}

From the emitter perspective, you don’t have to delete subscriptions directly. Redis’s channels are ambient: [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/16585161/redis-how-or-should-i-delete-pubsub-channels|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/16585161/redis-how-or-should-i-delete-pubsub-channels|smart-link] 

From the persistence perspective, the situation is more complicated. 
There is sense to consider 2 cases:

* You don’t use persistent sessions.
Subscriptions are stored in memory only. When client disconnects all subscription are erased.
* You use persistent sessions.
Subscriptions are stored forever. To unsubscribe, you have to unsubscribe a client directly.

Retained messages are stored in a separate Redis map “retained “, with key = topic, value = message. If I checked correctly, retained messages don't expire by ttl. They live until you remove them. 

One more thing. It looks like a client has a limit of 42 messages in a queue.

[~accountid:62d7b457807cf6f78ca9d117] regarding the added 4.2: 

This conflicts with T&C-s clause 4.1 which states that parties act as separate data controllers. 

Therefore would push back with the following explanation: 

Bolt and Customer are deemed as separate data controllers under the Agreement (T&C-s clause 4.1). Therefore Bolt does not process the data of end users on behalf of the Customer as a processor, but as an individual data controller in order to provide services to the end users under the applicable Terms of Service.

If the Customer wishes to conclude a separate agreement regarding data processing between individual controllers, then we can use Bolt’s Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) (added to the ticket). 

The fact that one organisation provides a service to another organisation does not necessarily mean that it is acting as a data processor. It could be a data controller in its own right, depending on the degree of control it exercises over the processing operation. Bolt as a controller decides the means and purposes for processing the data in order to provide the service (Bolt Business to the Customer). Bolt is the one registering and administering the users, providing the platform, providing the opportunity for end-users to make use of Bolt Business in the limits set by Customers. Therefore the data being shared is for each parties separate purposes - Bolt determines the means and purposes in order to provide the services and Customer determines the means and purposes of the shared data on how to manage their accounting purposes for business rides. 

Such conclusion and approach is also reflected in the guidance of [European Data Protection Board Guidelines|https://edpb.europa.eu/system/files/2021-07/eppb_guidelines_202007_controllerprocessor_final_en.pdf] (see p 82).

The external lawyer has responded to the follow up questions we raised last week, namely 

i) confirmation of a specific time limit within which we can pass on the fine to the user from the notification of the fine (i.e. 20 days, 1 month, etc.), and  

ii) whether it is possible to collect from the user those fines that we contest or whether we should wait for the outcome of the appeal.



Regarding the first question, the external lawyer advises that fines *should be communicated to the user as soon as they are received, so that the user has the possibility to pay them with the reduction.*

Regarding the second question, the external lawyer says that it would be advisable *to wait for the resolution of the allegations before charging the amount of the fines* (plus administrative costs) to the user's account.

On the other hand, it should be noted that the product lawyer's advice is to give the user *14 days' notice* before charging the fine.



Taking into account the above advice, the way to proceed should be as follows:

# If the operations team considers that a fine has been correctly issued and it appears to be the user's fault:
## Bolt pays the fine with the reduction within the voluntary deadline (20 days from the notification) and 
## Bolt announces to the user that the fine will be collected after 14 days and charges the fine to the user after the 14 day period has elapsed.
# If the operations team considers that the fine can be appealed -> Bolt lodges an appeal for reconsideration within one month of notification of the fine and waits for the result. If the City Council rejects the appeal (silently or expressly), 
## Bolt pays the fine (the full amount, as the discount is no longer applied).
## Bolt announces to the user that a fine will be charged after 14 days and charges the full amount after 14 days.

Hi Raphael and Quentin, 

According to [~accountid:61addb80b0b630006a695081] : the EE approach is that we will claim the user for the full damages and contractual penalty for not reporting the incident.

However, under FR law you can *EITHER* claim the full damage (before a court) *OR* the contractual penalties. You cannot cumulate both of them. 

If you think it is not worth claiming contractual penalties, then we can nevertheless align on EE process to determine the amount of the damage and recover it. 

In EE → in those cases, where the vehicle is totalled (as here), the damage claim is calculated based on this formula: market value of the vehicle - selling price of the wreck = amount claimed from the user. 

The process as it is now:

# Contacting the user
# Issuing an invoice to state the value : in EE the invoice is issues by the Bolt entity operating the service. in FR the best option would be to have an invoice/statement issued by a third party which has authority to impartially determine the damage suffered. 
# Sending reminders
# Outsourcing the damage claim: please sync with EE teams to see if you can rely on the same provider we use in EE [https://okincure.ee/en/|https://okincure.ee/en/] . Please keep me posted if we need to negotiate some contractual amendments. 
# Court.

Is user if not willing to pay the damages and we will need to go to court for enforcement measures.  

Damages in instalments (4k EUR over 12 months, for example) can be an option also. 

Hope this helps.

Hi [~accountid:5f0c30effe23000022252e68] and [~accountid:61124fbaec92ab0070270a0b] - I’ve double-checked with SPASS and we agree on the following conclusion:

* We think that, in an abstract way, it can be possible to have two policies. However, insurance companies may have a different understanding and perhaps, in practice, this is a situation that does not occur.
* Compulsory insurance covers damage suffered by third parties while driving (_eg_: a TVDE driver runs over a pedestrian on a crosswalk).  On the other hand, TVDE insurance is an activity insurance, which covers, for example, damage to the driver himself and the occupants of the vehicle.
* The essential thing is to understand the scope of insurance and the causes of exclusion of liability, so that there is no room for failure.
* If it turns out, in practice, that it is not possible to have two insurances, in that case the “contrato de comodato” should be excluded and the TVDE operator should be the owner, usufructuary or financial lessee.

Hope this clarifies this subject and all is now clear. Thank you.
